records.name: Ceara
records.summary:
For a trans visitor the operative risk in Ceará is sustained lethal exposure: the jurisdiction recorded 11 killings of trans and travesti people in 2024 — the region's highest toll and third nationally — and 8 in 2025, tied for the highest state total of that year's 80 nationwide; two consecutive years at the top of the ranking indicate an entrenched environment rather than a statistical blip. There is no state-level legal distinction: the national constitution and penal code apply uniformly.

The national victim profile sharpens the exposure for a visibly trans traveller: 97% of victims are travestis and trans women, over half aged 18–29, 70% of those with recorded race are Black, 97% killed in public spaces with most incidents outside capitals.

sources.summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (404; the URL carries dashes where the date segment expects slashes); the underlying G1/Globo report (28 Jan 2025) says Ceará was the Northeast state with the most killings of trans people in 2024 (11 killings, third nationally) according to the ANTRA dossier.

Igbá Agência (26 Jan 2026): per the 9th ANTRA dossier, Ceará was among the states with most trans killings in 2025 with 8 cases; Brazil totalled 80 (18th year as world's highest). Among 57 victims with race data, 70% were Black (avg 77% over 2017-2025).

SBT News (26 Jan 2026): ANTRA 9th dossier — Ceará and Minas Gerais topped the 2025 state ranking with 8 killings each; Brazil's 80 total down 34% vs 2024, still 1st worldwide; 1,261 killings 2017-2025 (avg 140/yr).

records.name: Rio Granda do Norte
records.summary:
The risk signal for this jurisdiction is a violence-rate spike: zero recorded trans killings in 2024 jumped to 4 in 2025 — the sharpest deterioration in the dataset. Against a population of ~3.5 million, four cases yield approximately 1.14 killings per million per year, the highest per-capita rate among all 27 units in 2025 and roughly three times the national figure of ~0.38/million. The dataset cautions against reading a single-year zero as safety and notes the volatility.

For a visitor, the small absolute numbers mean a single incident dramatically shifts perception, and the volatility suggests the environment can turn rapidly. No state-level statutory restriction or unique legal finding applies; the risk is purely a violence-rate signal.

sources.summary: Sergipe em Debate report (27 Jan 2025) on the ANTRA dossier for 2024: 122 trans and travesti killings (16% down from 145 in 2023, close to the 125/year 2008-2024 average), five of them human-rights defenders, 95.9% of victims travestis/trans women, and systematic under-counting because official bodies do not record LGBTQIA+ victims properly — the dossier basis for Rio Grande do Norte appearing with zero recorded killings in 2024 before jumping to 4 in 2025.

SBT News report on the 9th ANTRA dossier (2025 data): Brazil 80 killings, 18th straight year topping the global tally; the state ranking places Ceará and Minas Gerais top with 8 each, while Paraíba and Rio Grande do Norte appear with 4 each — RN's jump from zero in 2024 makes it the sharpest deterioration in the dataset; the Northeast recorded 38 of the 80 killings.

Saiba Mais (RN) reports that in the early hours of 4 May 2026 a 27-year-old transgender woman, Emanuelle Samira Fernandes Neta, was shot dead inside her rented home on Rua Vivaldo Dantas in the Dom Jaime Câmara neighbourhood of Mossoró, western Rio Grande do Norte, after five men broke in and executed her while she slept; military police found the body on a routine patrol, and one suspect was arrested with a pistol and booked for illegal firearms discharge and armed criminal association. RN trans-rights group ATTRANSPARÊNCIA/RN publicly mourned Samira as an artist killed by the transphobia she faced. The case documents lethal violence against trans women in Rio Grande do Norte continuing after the years this record covers, matching the record's warning that a single-year zero should not be read as safety.

Saiba Mais (RN) reports that a transgender woman known as Naomi was found dead inside her own home in Praia da Pipa, Tibau do Sul municipality on the southern coast of Rio Grande do Norte, killed by stab wounds in late February 2026, with the Civil Police opening an investigation and RN trans-rights association ATTRANSPARÊNCIA/RN calling for justice. The same article reproduces the ANTRA 2025 dossier figures: 80 trans killings in Brazil in 2025 (a 34% drop from 2024), 38 of them in the Nordeste, and zero registered trans killings in Rio Grande do Norte in 2025 — a count that conflicts with this record's stated 4 killings for the state in 2025 and needs reconciliation in rework.
